scope: Read-only review of shared geometry, native and web Radar components, theme recipes, galleries, and focused tests. No production files changed.
decision: Suitable for a bounded synthetic UI handoff; not ready to present real observations until axis comparability and caller authority are explicit.

claims.claim: Measure and perspective selection are separate and the UI does not average them or combine multiple observations into one chart.
Null is retained as missing rather than converted to zero; incomplete observations do not produce a closed polygon, and fewer than three axes do not produce a chart.

Web and native provide readable values and ranges outside the chart; access-denied and other non-ready states do not render observation details. Synthetic fixtures are labeled, and the web gallery is production guarded.
The shared geometry is platform-neutral and color/stroke choices come from world radar recipes; component placement follows native/web package boundaries.
Accessible equivalents are present in unit-rendered markup, but this review does not establish screen-reader behavior, browser layout, or native device rendering.

findings.finding: Geometry independently maps each axis from its own min/max onto the same 0..1 radial distance, then draws a polygon when all axes have values. The contract permits each axis to have a different unit, and neither geometry nor adapters require compatible units or an explicitly comparable measure. A chart can therefore visually compare incompatible quantities despite preserving their individual ranges in the table.
findings.recommended_resolution: Require a measure-owned plot/comparability policy before drawing a normalized shape, or render only the value/range table when axis scales are not declared comparable. Keep distinct measures and perspectives isolated.

findings.finding: A ready observation with an empty axes array passes validation and returns ready with plot=false. Components then show metadata and an empty value table instead of the explicit empty state. Missing values are also represented by a single null, so the component cannot distinguish not collected, unavailable, or intentionally withheld per axis.
Web displays perspective.kind (self/observer) alongside its label; native displays the perspective label only. A caller can use a vague label, leaving the explicit attribution kind absent on native.

The UI accepts caller-supplied subject and source metadata and does not establish authorization, provenance, or data isolation. Denied-state rendering is tested, but access control must be enforced by the host data adapter before constructing ready state.

The native test passed with the general mock-engine config. vitest.native.config.mts has an explicit include list of five different tests, so Radar is not in the native real-runtime lane. The mobile gallery source provides a synthetic fixture only; no device run was performed here.

commands.result: passed: 2 files, 11 tests; vitest-native engine mock, iOS platform
passed: 1 file, 9 tests; DOM unit tests, explicitly labeled no browser layout evidence

not_verified: Live person data, authorization, or data-source provenance
